principles.title: Fail-closed by default
principles.statement: When the system can't verify a condition, it must refuse rather than guess. Authorization, cache misses and unknown tool intents all default to 'no'.
principles.example: In mscodebase-intelligence, a missing index returns a structured error to the agent instead of an empty result — the agent must not confuse 'nothing found' with 'index empty'.
principles.abTest: If we returned empty results on index-miss: agents would silently produce 'no results' for every query until the index rebuilt — a 30-minute silent outage instead of an immediate actionable error.
principles.evidence: mscodebase-intelligence: watchdog + reindex recovery paths surface explicit statuses

principles.title: Async-first I/O, offload CPU
principles.statement: I/O-bound work lives on the async loop; CPU-bound work is offloaded with explicit progress reporting. No blocking calls on the request path.
principles.example: The MCP tool server is fully async; reindex runs as a background task with progress notifications so the agent can poll instead of timing out.
principles.abTest: A sync reindex inside a tool call would blow the MCP request timeout on large repos — the async split is what makes 100k-file codebases viable.
principles.evidence: mscodebase-intelligence architecture (async MCP server, background jobs)

principles.title: Single write path for derived state
principles.statement: Any state that is derived from other state (indexes, caches, fused rankings) is written through one code path. No ad-hoc mutations.
principles.example: Hybrid search keeps a vector index and a BM25 index consistent because both are updated by the same ingestion pipeline.
principles.abTest: Two ad-hoc update sites would drift: vector index fresh, BM25 stale → fusion ranks garbage without any visible error.

principles.title: Measure, don't assume
principles.statement: Performance and reliability claims come from benchmarks with a command line, a thread count and raw output — not from architecture diagrams.
principles.example: Every concurrency change in mscodebase-intelligence ships with a stress test that verifies both 'no exceptions' and 'correct input → correct output'.
principles.abTest: Lock→pool refactors without content-correctness stress tests have historically passed '0 errors' while silently cross-wiring results.
principles.evidence: mscodebase-intelligence test suite: N=2 and N=8 concurrency stress tests

principles.title: Autonomous self-healing
principles.statement: Where recovery is deterministic, the system does it itself: watchdogs, reindex triggers, stale-state cleanup. Humans only get involved for decisions, not for chores.
principles.example: MSCodeBase Intelligence detects a corrupted/stale index and schedules a reindex automatically while serving from the last-good snapshot.
principles.abTest: A human-paged reindex flow means the tool is down on a Friday night until someone notices — unacceptable for a developer tool.

principles.title: Agent-agnostic surfaces
principles.statement: Tooling speaks protocols (MCP), not personalities. One server, consumed by Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or any future agent.
principles.example: This portfolio's own MCP server speaks standard Streamable HTTP — the same endpoint works from Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot with zero per-IDE setup.
principles.abTest: IDE-specific plugins would multiply maintenance by N and make the tool useless the day a new IDE appears.
